title: Cash withdrawals dispersed across many ATMs in a wide geography
definition: Cash withdrawals made from a large number of automated teller machines spread across a wide area, within a short period, at a rate above the account's usual withdrawal pattern. The indicator measures dispersion and rate; it does not establish why the money was withdrawn.
evidence_to_cite: the withdrawal records, each cited by its own source id and pointer
the terminal identifiers and their locations
the account's historical withdrawal pattern, over a stated period
benign_explanations: A traveller or a seasonal worker withdrawing cash in the places they visit.
A business that pays out daily cash to several sites and withdraws at the nearest terminal.
A customer who uses different terminals to avoid a per-terminal daily limit, as a matter of convenience.
Cash-intensive work, such as market trading or event staffing, paid partly in cash.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, currency transaction reporting and aggregation guidance, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
